name: US dollar
summary: Dollar index near 103.7 on 23 Nov, close to its 52-week high and about 4.6% higher over three months
state: The DXY dollar index was near 103.7 early on 23 Nov, a fraction below its 52-week high of 103.9 and 4.6% higher over three months, just under the 5% Watch line, which it touched on 20 Nov (Yahoo Finance). The level is inside the 90–108 range, and SOFR stayed within 3bp of the Fed's reserve rate over five days (FRED), so no dollar funding stress is visible. Watch is kept under hysteresis while the dollar sits at its high.
for_you: A strong dollar raises the cost of dollar-priced imports such as oil for other economies and tightens conditions for dollar borrowers abroad.
rubric_hit: DXY 3m move 4.76% has not yet cleared the 4.5% exit line, so Watch holds
why: The dollar is the world's funding currency; violent moves squeeze emerging markets and anyone with dollar debts.
drivers: Fed vs other central banks, safe-haven demand, trade policy, reserve diversification.

rubric.alert: DXY moved > 8% in 3 months, or dollar funding stress (Fed swap lines drawn materially).
rubric.watch: DXY moved 5–8% in 3 months, or outside 90–108.
rubric.normal: DXY moved < 5% over 3 months and is between 90 and 108.
